Traced the historical intervention. All seeded memories share the BENCH_TAG, while run_consolidation clusters by any tag overlap; therefore all 72 smoke-trial episodic memories form one qualifying cluster, one semantic record is created, and all 72 originals are marked Consolidated. The generated semantic content concatenates every member content and metadata stores consolidated_from member IDs. This structurally explains 72->1 for the checked scenario and must not be generalized to learned semantic consolidation.

Exact input-byte and receiver-row replay is therefore impossible from the package alone.

The historical benchmark executes lifecycle::run_consolidation, which at the checked revision writes the derived memory/relations and updates originals but does not emit a MemoryConsolidated AgentEvent. Current v0.5 query::consolidate is a separate deterministic by-id primitive that preserves member provenance and emits hash-chained MemoryConsolidated/MemoryRevised events; it is useful as a packaging reference but cannot retroactively attest the historical benchmark path.

new_findings.summary: mnemo provides a stronger-than-paper-only static package: a GitHub-verified merge revision co-locates the Auto-Dreamer-style benchmark source with committed per-trial/aggregate result artifacts. Scheduled Chat can recompute the published 72->1 ratio and aggregate arithmetic without executing the benchmark, but this is aggregate/reducer verification rather than full run replay.

For the checked 3x6x12 smoke configuration, the 72->1 active-bank collapse is structurally induced by the benchmark's shared BENCH_TAG plus historical tag-overlap clustering: every active episodic memory enters one cluster, one concatenating semantic record is created and all 72 originals become Consolidated. Interpret this as a shape/mechanism benchmark, not learned optimal semantic abstraction.

The committed mnemo package omits exact per-run inputs and receiver rows: needles use Uuid::now_v7(), timestamps use Utc::now(), and generated IDs/timestamps plus ordered pre/post retrieval result IDs/content hashes are not serialized. Thus result arithmetic is statically checkable but exact input-byte/retrieval replay is not.

There is an audit-plane execution-path gap: historical lifecycle::run_consolidation used by the benchmark emits no MemoryConsolidated AgentEvent at the checked revision. Current v0.5 deterministic query::consolidate does emit hash-chained consolidation/revision events with member provenance, but it is a sibling/newer path and cannot attest the historical run.

Public CI does not independently corroborate PR #96's self-reported local green smoke run: both CI and security workflows on the only PR feature commit concluded failure, with Test/Build/Clippy/Security Audit failed and no Actions artifacts. Failure cause is unresolved, so do not infer the benchmark result itself is false.
